delivery-lead.value: Creates a bounded, reviewable decision artifact while keeping scope, authority, evidence, and unresolved questions explicit and separate from approval.
delivery-lead.risk: The goal is not implementable or approvable until viewport definitions, decision-state semantics, accessibility target, evidence-link behavior, controlled-session boundary, and named owners for open items are recorded; completion or agent consensus must not be treated as approval.
dependencies: Manager approval of a versioned charter before implementation

acceptanceCriteria: A versioned charter records the candidate goal, scope, exclusions, authority, decision owner, date, and basis for each decision.
The component presents one project decision with evidence links, severity, due date, and explicit acknowledge and defer actions, including defined behavior for each state.
Behavioral requirements have deterministic RED then GREEN evidence, including failure evidence and relevant negative paths.
Accessibility is objectively tested against a recorded target, including keyboard operation, focus visibility, semantics, and status/action announcements where applicable.
Current-build visual evidence covers the manager-approved viewports and identifies the exact build under review.
The component remains isolated from unfinished production UI and all work stays within the controlled session with no external side effects.
An independent release review records needs-work or eligible-for-owner-approval; neither result is treated as manager approval.
Every open item remains visible with a named owner, and no scope exception is closed without required access or written acknowledgement.
evidenceNeeds: Versioned charter with decision log, authorities, timestamps, rationale, and disagreement register
Reconciled constraints and explicit scope/exclusions

Deterministic browser outputs, including failure evidence

Which browser, viewport dimensions, and visual-review tolerances are approved?
What accessibility conformance target and assistive-technology coverage are required?
How should evidence links behave when absent, invalid, or unavailable without network access?

No role consensus, passing check, or release-review outcome can substitute for manager approval or close an unresolved scope exception.

product-designer.goal: Build an isolated Decision Notice component with a versioned interaction and art-direction contract: present one decision's title, rationale/evidence links, severity, due date, and clearly distinct Acknowledge and Defer actions; support keyboard, screen-reader, focus, validation, and deterministic visual review without implying completion equals approval.
product-designer.value: Contract: use a single bounded notice surface with semantic heading, decision summary, severity badge whose text is never color-only, localized/explicit due-date text, evidence links that expose destination or purpose, and action controls with visible focus. Acknowledge requires an observable confirmed state; Defer requires an explicit defer reason or date and preserves the decision context. State transitions must be deterministic, reversible only where specified, and must not trigger network or production side effects. Anti-goals: no dashboard, decision editing, authentication, real persistence, notifications, analytics, external navigation during tests, or invented evidence. Deferrals: responsive behavior beyond the approved viewport set and localization are deferred until 2026-09-20, explicitly excluded from this charter rather than inferred as complete.
product-designer.risk: The briefing does not specify approved viewport dimensions, severity taxonomy, due-date timezone/format, defer semantics, evidence-link destinations, or whether acknowledgement is reversible; choosing these silently could create an unapproved product contract.
dependencies: Manager-approved versioned charter and surface specification
Owner decision on severity values, due-date format/timezone, acknowledgement/defer semantics, and approved viewports
Deterministic fixture data and controlled-session browser harness
Independent visual and release review
acceptanceCriteria: At the approved viewports, exactly one Decision Notice is visible with a unique accessible name, title, decision summary, severity, due date, and at least one evidence link when fixture data provides one.
Severity is conveyed by text and not color alone; due date is presented in an unambiguous human-readable format; links identify their destination or purpose.
All interactive elements are keyboard reachable in a logical order, have visible focus, and expose correct accessible names, roles, and states; automated checks alone are insufficient evidence.
Activating Acknowledge produces a deterministic, visibly distinct acknowledged state and does not perform network, persistence, deployment, publishing, or other external side effects.

Activating Defer presents the contractually defined defer input/state; incomplete or invalid input is visibly identified and does not transition; valid input produces a deterministic deferred state retaining the decision context.
Browser tests include RED evidence for each new behavioral assertion, GREEN evidence after implementation, deterministic failure evidence, and current-build screenshots at every approved viewport.
Visual findings are recorded against named art-direction clauses, and independent release review returns needs-work or eligible-for-owner-approval; neither result is treated as owner approval.

RED/GREEN behavioral test artifacts and deterministic browser failure evidence

test-engineer.goal: Build the isolated Decision Notice only after defining a versioned acceptance contract that specifies deterministic rendering, evidence-link behavior, severity and due-date semantics, acknowledge/defer state transitions, and accessible interaction outcomes.

delivery-lead.statement: The synthesis accurately preserves the seed, constraints, dissent, and evidence gaps. Amend the proposed goal to state that every unresolved gap remains open with a named owner and blocks implementation or release eligibility until resolved or explicitly accepted by the authorized manager; this clarifies ownership and prevents the charter from being mistaken for approval.

product-designer.statement: The synthesis accurately preserves the blocking design uncertainties and evidence boundaries. Amend the proposed goal to require the approved charter to include an explicit art-direction contract, observable state-by-state acceptance criteria, anti-goals, and named dated deferrals; otherwise visual/content behavior could remain implicitly in scope despite the listed gaps. Implementation must remain blocked until those contract clauses, approved viewport/browser matrix, and owner/manager authority are versioned.

implementation-engineer.statement: I affirm the synthesis and its implementation gate, but amend the contract to make the pre-implementation sequence explicit: first approve the versioned charter and fixture/schema, then record RED evidence for each behavioral criterion, implement the smallest isolated change, capture GREEN and deterministic browser failure evidence, and only then collect current-build visual evidence. Until the manager resolves the listed schema, interaction, link-safety, viewport/browser, accessibility, and provenance gaps, implementation remains blocked; no visual artifact should be treated as current-build evidence before a defined build exists.

test-engineer.statement: The synthesis is directionally sound, but amend the goal to require a criterion-to-test traceability matrix and an explicit testability gate: no criterion is satisfied without fixed expected assertions, RED/GREEN provenance, rejection-path coverage, and deterministic failure evidence. Resolve the listed semantics and environment matrix before implementation; otherwise tests cannot establish the claimed behavior, and skipped or gated checks must remain not performed rather than passing.

visual-qa-reviewer.statement: I affirm the synthesis. It correctly preserves the visual-QA boundary: no visual fidelity or approval claim can rely on DOM snapshots, state probes, automated diffs, or passing tests alone. Before implementation or visual review, amend the charter with the named viewport/browser/device matrix, versioned art-direction and complete state contract, capture and console/network procedures, and explicit marking of every unverified condition; visual review may provide evidence and discrepancies only, while owner approval remains separate.

release-reviewer.statement: The synthesis preserves the release-review mandate: all listed evidence gaps remain blocking until resolved in a manager-approved, versioned charter and established by revision-matched artifacts. It correctly requires provenance, supersession tracking, failure-path evidence, isolation verification, and independent review while limiting the review conclusion to needs-work or eligible-for-owner-approval. This affirmation is agreement with the synthesis, not approval of the charter or certification of any implementation.

synthesis.proposedGoal: Retain and revise the Decision Notice seed into a manager-approval-gated, versioned charter and acceptance contract for an isolated, accessible component presenting exactly one authoritative decision with traceable evidence links, severity, due date, and deterministic acknowledge/defer outcomes; require criterion-linked RED/GREEN behavioral evidence, deterministic success and failure browser evidence, current-build visual evidence at explicitly approved viewports and browsers, accessibility verification, isolation/no-side-effect verification, artifact provenance and supersession tracking, and an independent release review that concludes only needs-work or eligible-for-owner-approval.

disagreementRegister.statement: Implementation must remain blocked until manager approval of a versioned charter; consensus, passing checks, completion, or release review cannot substitute for approval or close scope exceptions.

The seed is not implementation-ready until interaction semantics, visual contract, viewport set, severity, due-date rules, evidence-link behavior, and anti-goals are explicitly decided and versioned; unstated defaults must not count as satisfied requirements.
Visual evidence and a green suite are evidence inputs only, not approval; implementation requires an approved contract, deterministic fixtures, controlled-session adapters, and independent review.
A passing suite, DOM snapshot, or state probe cannot establish visual correctness; required tests may not be skipped or gated, and RED/GREEN provenance plus rejection-path coverage are mandatory.

DOM snapshots, state probes, automated diffs, or passing tests alone cannot prove visual fidelity or design approval; all named states, viewports, browsers, device classes, and deviations must be explicitly evidenced or marked unverified.

The seed is inadequate as an acceptance contract; unanswered questions and unexamined required inputs remain blocking open obligations, and release review may return only needs-work or eligible-for-owner-approval, never approval.

payload.goal: Build the isolated Decision Notice only after defining a versioned acceptance contract that specifies deterministic rendering, evidence-link behavior, severity and due-date semantics, acknowledge/defer state transitions, and accessible interaction outcomes.
payload.value: Require TDD evidence for each behavioral change: a recorded RED failure followed by GREEN, fixed expected assertions, deterministic fixtures, and explicit negative-case coverage. Test keyboard-only operation, focus visibility/order, accessible names and state announcements, invalid or missing decision data, unavailable evidence links, and mutually exclusive acknowledge/defer actions. Treat skipped or gated checks as not performed.
payload.risk: A green suite may provide false confidence if assertions restate inputs, omit rejection paths, or test only internal state rather than user-visible behavior. Browser checks and DOM/state probes cannot establish visual correctness.
dependencies: Manager-approved versioned charter and acceptance contract
Stable fixture schema for decision, evidence links, severity, due date, and action state
Defined semantics for acknowledge versus defer, including repeated actions and persistence scope
Approved browser/viewports and a deterministic test harness
acceptanceCriteria: Every behavioral requirement has a fixed expected assertion and a demonstrated RED-then-GREEN record
At least one negative test exists for each input or transition that must be rejected
The component is operable and understandable via keyboard and assistive-technology-relevant accessibility assertions
Fixtures produce repeatable results without live-provider or network calls
Acknowledge and defer outcomes are distinguishable, mutually defined, and correctly reject invalid transitions
Test reports separately identify passed, failed, skipped, and not-performed checks
Visual approval relies on current-build visual evidence reviewed independently, not on automated test output
evidenceNeeds: RED output showing each new test failed for the stated reason
GREEN output from the same deterministic tests
Count and inventory of negative cases
Browser failure evidence for rejected interactions and accessibility violations
Fixture and environment details proving no network or external side effects
Independent current-build visual evidence at approved viewports
uncertainties: Whether acknowledge/defer state is session-only or must survive reload
What constitutes a valid, unavailable, or malformed evidence link
How due dates are formatted and handled across timezone boundaries
Required severity vocabulary and behavior for unknown severity
Which accessibility conformance target and assistive technology checks are required
disagreements: I disagree with treating a passing build, unit suite, DOM snapshot, or state probe as proof of visual correctness; visual claims require separate current-build evidence.
I would not accept completion while any required test is skipped or gated, or while RED/GREEN provenance is absent.
